# VRFComponentEditor

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Core.Editors.UI` · assembly `VRFramework.Core.Editors` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Editor/UI/VRFComponentEditor.cs#L20)

Base class for the framework's inspectors. It draws the shared header, keeps the
serializedObject bookkeeping in one place, and hands subclasses the helpers they need to
stay correct when several objects are selected at once.

Multi-object editing is the reason this class exists. The rule it enforces is simple:
write through [`SerializedProperty`](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/SerializedProperty.html) only. Assigning to
`(MyComponent)target`writes to whichever object happens to be first in the
selection and silently drops the rest, which is what made the old inspectors
single-select. Reading from [`targets`](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/Editor.targets.html) is fine, and
[`AnyTarget<T>(Func<T, bool>)`](/api/vrframework-core-editors-ui/VRFComponentEditor#anytarget-1-boolean) exists for exactly that.

```csharp
public abstract class VRFComponentEditor : Editor
```

### AnyTarget\<T>(Func\<T, bool>) {#anytarget-1-boolean}

True when at least one selected object satisfies the predicate. This is how conditional
sections stay useful in a mixed selection: a field is shown when it is relevant to
anything selected, instead of vanishing the moment two objects disagree.

```csharp
protected bool AnyTarget<T>(Func<T, bool> predicate) where T : class
```

### Prop(string) {#prop-string}

Cached [`SerializedProperty`](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/SerializedProperty.html) by field name. Logs once and returns null for a
name that does not exist, so a renamed field shows up as a missing row rather than a
NullReferenceException every repaint.
